newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bosnia leaders urged to comply with peace accord.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia leaders urged to comply with peace accord.

text.p: The multinational Contact Group on former Yugoslavia accused authorities in Bosnia on Thursday of failing to comply with the Bosnian peace agreement.

"The Contact Group...expressed serious concern at the lack of determination by the authorities in Bosnia and Herzegovina to honour their own commitments," it said in a statement after a meeting in Brussels.

The Contact Group comprises the international community's High Representative for Bosnia Carl Bildt and senior officials of Britain, France, Germany, Italy, Russia, the United States and the Netherlands as European Union president.

It said Bosnian authorities failed to cooperate sufficiently not only with the U.N. war crimes tribunal in The Hague but also on areas such as respect for human rights, the rule of law and the right of refugees to return freely.
It said the authorities also cooperated insufficiently in ensuring freedom of movement, communication and the press.

They also fell short in adopting and implementing economic laws and regulations needed for the functioning of Bosnia as a single state, such as a common currency and customs regulations, the statement said.

The Contact Group meeting was called to prepare a ministerial meeting of the Peace Implementation Council (PIC) Steering Board, which oversees the Bosnian peace settlement, in Sintra, Portugal, on May 30.

The statement said the international community demanded in exchange for its high level of support that all parties would accept their responsibility for implementing and abiding by the peace treaty commitments.
